question: On exact current product source and one hosted runner, does the canonical performance worker path materially increase the accepted-v0.29→v0.30 ML create ratio relative to the older v2 worker path, when both time the same engine.build calls on one deterministic ML source tree?
mechanism_hypothesis: The canonical worker imports the canonical v0.30 product identity engine before starting its operation timer even when measuring v0.29. The v2 worker does not. That pre-timer import can warm current-product/shared dependencies for the v0.29 baseline without equivalently helping v0.30, making the canonical v0.30/v0.29 ratio worse even though engine.build semantics are unchanged.

prediction.primary: The same-run conventional median canonical-worker create ratio will exceed the same-run v2-worker ratio on ML.
prediction.stronger_signal: If canonical median is >1.25 while v2 median is <=1.25, wrapper/worker custody rather than product-source lineage is sufficient to explain the release-gate split.
prediction.falsifier: If the two worker paths have materially overlapping paired ratios and the canonical-v2 median delta is not directionally positive, this worker-path hypothesis is not the runtime owner.

court.source_tree: neutral_hostile_v1/09_ml_artifacts generated once by the current frozen corpus builder and reused by all arms
court.statistic: For each worker path, compute four per-pair v030/v029 pack_wall ratios and the conventional even-sample median (mean of the middle two sorted ratios).
court.charge: Each worker is invoked as its unchanged fresh Python subprocess. Worker import/setup before its own operation timer remains exactly whatever that worker currently owns; parent orchestration time is not credited.
identity: same deterministic source tree SHA-256 domain
same v0.29 archive bytes across both worker paths
same v0.30 archive bytes across both worker paths
same per-engine tree identity across both worker paths

credit_boundary: Research/custody attribution only. A result does not change product code, release thresholds, candidate fingerprint authority, or grant release credit.
next_if_positive: Localize the smallest worker-path cause, beginning with canonical worker's unconditional pre-timer product-identity import on v0.29, then rerun the unchanged release-performance court only after a causal repair.
next_if_negative: Do not tune the worker path. Return to the already-preregistered same-run historical-current source replay or the next strongest runtime owner test.
safety: No archive format, selector, workload, comparator, threshold, integrity, recovery, path, locality, timing boundary inside either worker, or release law is modified.
